text.p: These are the leading stories in the Belgrade press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified them nor does it vouch for their accuracy.
- Hundreds of thousands of Belgraders celebrate Orthodox New Year in the city centre. Rally organised by student protesters and the opposition coalition Zajedno.
- Association of free and independent trade unions (ASNS) calls on all unions to meet and discuss problems facing workers and possible ways of solving them other than strikes.
- The National Bank of Yugoslavia auctioned a new 20 million dinar tranche of its 30-day bonds on Monday at an annual 147.48 percent interest rate.
- Bakers to hold meeting in the Serbian trade ministry over abrupt rise of wheat and flour price on the domestic market.
- Opposition coalition Zajedno leaders to visit Rome on January 17.
- Serbian Justice Ministry warns electoral commission in Nis to determine without delay final results for the city assembly.
- New commander of U.N. forces in Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES) Willy Hanset says he will do everything to carry out his task and prevent incidents in the region.
- Serbian Deputy Prime Minister Slobodan Radulovic says dinar exchange rate at 3.3 to 3.5 to the German mark is realistic but domestic prices are too high.
- Nis tobacco factory calls for measures to be taken against black market cigarette sales due to which it had sold 503 tonnes of cigarettes less in 1996 than in 1995.
- Serbian post and telecommunications PTT raises prices of subscription to five dinars from 2.67 as well as price of impulses.
- Belgrade University council upholds agreement between student protesters and Serbian government on respect of local election results.
- Tuesday evening panel discussion in Serbian parliament on local elections to be transmitted live by state TV. Opposition parties not participating.
